# package rt

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-profinet/rt"
```

Package rt implements cyclic real-time PROFINET IO (RT\_CLASS\_1/2, unsynchronized): the codec of cyclic frames, the layout of the IO data in a frame, providers and consumers with their watchdog, and the scheduler that drives them.

The cyclic frame is FrameID, the C\_SDU (the IO data objects with their provider status and the consumer status octets), CycleCounter, DataStatus and TransferStatus, on EtherType 0x8892 with an 802.1Q tag of priority 6.

Functional correctness on a virtual network does not establish real-time behaviour on hardware: see the measurements in docs/CYCLIC.md.

## Constants

```go
const (
	MinDataLength = 40
	MaxDataLength = 1440
	// TrailerLen is CycleCounter, DataStatus and TransferStatus.
	TrailerLen = 4
)
```

Limits of the C\_SDU.

```go
const (
	FrameIDUDPMin   uint16 = 0xC000
	FrameIDUDPMax   uint16 = 0xF7FF
	FrameIDUDPMCMin uint16 = 0xF800
	FrameIDUDPMCMax uint16 = 0xFBFF
)
```

FrameID ranges of RT\_CLASS\_UDP, as Wireshark labels them: 0xC000-0xF7FF unicast, 0xF800-0xFBFF multicast.

```go
const CycleUnit = 31250 // nanoseconds
```

CycleUnit is the unit of SendClockFactor and of the cycle counter.

```go
const DefaultDataStatus = StatePrimary | DataValid | ProviderRun | StationOK
```

DefaultDataStatus is primary, valid, running and without a station problem (0x35).

```go
const MinDataLengthUDP = 12
```

MinDataLengthUDP is the smallest C\_SDU of an RT\_CLASS\_UDP IOCR. Without Ethernet padding, the 40 octets of RT\_CLASS\_1 do not apply; p-net accepts 12..1440 for RT\_CLASS\_UDP (observed in that implementation, which cites the PROFINET protocol specification).

```go
const UDPPort = 0x8892
```

UDPPort is the UDP destination port of RT\_CLASS\_UDP frames (34962).

```go
const VLANPriority = 6
```

VLANPriority is the 802.1Q priority of cyclic RT frames.


Consumer receives the cyclic frames of one IOCR, keeps the newest C\_SDU and watches the data hold time.

#### func NewConsumer

NewConsumer returns a consumer. Its startup grace starts now; the data hold watchdog with the first frame.

#### func (Consumer) Arm

```go
func (c *Consumer) Arm(now time.Time)
```

Arm ends the startup grace: from now, the data hold time applies even when no frame has arrived yet. The owner calls it once the AR is established, when the provider must be sending.

#### func (Consumer) Check

```go

```

Check reports whether the watchdog expired at now. It returns true once per expiry; a frame that arrives afterwards re-arms it.

### type ConsumerConfig

```go
type ConsumerConfig struct {
	FrameID    uint16
	DataLength uint16
	// Src is the provider's MAC address; frames from other addresses are
	// counted and dropped. Zero accepts any source.
	Src ethernet.MAC
	// Watchdog is the data hold time: once the first frame arrived, the
	// consumer expires when no valid frame arrives for this long.
	Watchdog time.Duration
	// StartupGrace bounds the wait for the first frame: providers start
	// at different points of the AR establishment (p-net, for one, only
	// after ApplicationReady). Zero waits without bound; the AR's own
	// timeouts then apply.
	StartupGrace time.Duration
}
```

### type DataStatus

```go
type DataStatus uint8
```

DataStatus is the APDU status octet of a cyclic frame.

```go
const (
	StatePrimary     DataStatus = 0x01
	Redundancy       DataStatus = 0x02
	DataValid        DataStatus = 0x04
	ProviderRun      DataStatus = 0x10
	StationOK        DataStatus = 0x20 // StationProblemIndicator: 1 = normal
	IgnoreDataStatus DataStatus = 0x80
)
```

DataStatus bits.

```go
const (
	RedundancyMask DataStatus = 0x07
	// Output CR (controller to device).
	PrimaryRequest DataStatus = 0x05
	BackupRequest  DataStatus = 0x04
	// Input CR (device to controller).
	PrimaryAck           DataStatus = 0x05
	BackupAckWithData    DataStatus = 0x04
	BackupAckWithoutData DataStatus = 0x00
	PrimaryMissingData   DataStatus = 0x06
	PrimaryMissingNoData DataStatus = 0x02
	PrimaryFault         DataStatus = 0x07
)
```

The DataStatus bits State, Redundancy and DataValid (mask 0x07) of an IOCARSR's frames: on the output CR the controller's request, on the input CR the device's acknowledgement (Wireshark's PNIO RT dissector).

### type Frame

```go
type Frame struct {
	FrameID        uint16
	Data           []byte
	CycleCounter   uint16
	DataStatus     DataStatus
	TransferStatus uint8
}
```

Frame is a decoded cyclic frame. Data aliases the decoded buffer.

#### func Decode

```go
func Decode(p []byte, dataLen int) (Frame, error)
```

Decode decodes the PROFINET payload (FrameID first) of a cyclic frame whose C\_SDU is dataLen octets long. A negative dataLen takes the C\_SDU to be everything between the FrameID and the trailer, which is right for frames of at least the minimum size.

#### func DecodeUDP

```go
func DecodeUDP(p []byte, dataLen int) (Frame, error)
```

DecodeUDP decodes the UDP payload of an RT\_CLASS\_UDP frame. The C\_SDU is the payload between the FrameID and the trailer: a datagram carries no padding, so with dataLen ≥ 0 the payload must be exactly 2 + dataLen + 4 octets. Data aliases p.

Layout is the arrangement of the C\_SDU of one IOCR.

#### func ComputeLayout

```go
func ComputeLayout(k pnio.IOCRType, subs []SubmoduleIO) (Layout, error)
```

ComputeLayout arranges the C\_SDU of an IOCR of kind k (IOCRInput or IOCROutput): the data objects in submodule order, each followed by its IOPS, then the IOCS octets. DataLength is at least MinDataLength.

#### func LayoutFromIOCR

```go
func LayoutFromIOCR(req *pnio.IOCRBlockReq, subs []SubmoduleIO) (Layout, error)
```

LayoutFromIOCR validates the offsets a controller put in an IOCR against the submodule shapes and returns the layout. Every data object and IOCS must lie inside DataLength and no two may overlap; a submodule that the IOCR does not list is left out of the layout.

### type ProviderConfig

```go
type ProviderConfig struct {
	FrameID    uint16
	DataLength uint16
	// Dst is the consumer's MAC address, Src the provider's.
	Dst, Src ethernet.MAC
	// VLAN is the VLAN id of the 802.1Q tag (priority 6); 0 sends
	// priority-tagged frames.
	VLAN uint16
	// CounterStep is SendClockFactor × ReductionRatio: the cycle counter
	// advances by it with every frame.
	CounterStep uint16
	// Send transmits a frame; it must not retain the buffer.
	Send func(ctx context.Context, frame []byte) error
	// Fill, when set, is called with the C_SDU before every frame, under
	// the provider's lock, to bring it up to date. It must not block or
	// retain the slice.
	Fill func(cSDU []byte)
}
```

ProviderConfig configures a [Provider](#type-provider).

### type Scheduler

```go
type Scheduler struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Scheduler runs periodic tasks on one goroutine, on deadlines derived from the monotonic clock (start + n × period, so that lateness does not accumulate as drift). A run that is late by more than a period skips the missed deadlines and counts them. Tasks must not block: they encode and send a frame, or check a watchdog.

A Scheduler is safe for concurrent use.

#### func NewScheduler

```go
func NewScheduler() *Scheduler
```

NewScheduler starts a scheduler.

#### func (Scheduler) Add

```go

```

Add schedules fn every period, first after one period.

#### func (Scheduler) Close

```go

```

Close stops the scheduler.

#### func (Scheduler) Remove

```go
func (s *Scheduler) Remove(t *Task)
```

Remove unschedules t. It does not wait for a run in progress, so it can be called from the task itself; a run that was starting while Remove was called may still happen once.

```go
type TaskStats struct {

	// Missed is the number of deadlines skipped because the scheduler was
```
